summary.one_liner: Vanna 2.0 is a Python framework for building natural-language-to-SQL agents that return SQL, tables, charts, and summaries, with user-aware permissions and a pre-built web chat component.
summary.what_it_does: Vanna lets users ask data questions in natural language and receive generated SQL, the query results as an interactive table, Plotly charts, and a natural-language summary, streamed in real time. It uses a user resolver to map incoming requests (cookies, JWTs, or other auth) to a user identity and group memberships, which the README says drive row-level filtering and permission checks on tools. Developers can register custom tools by extending a Tool base class with access-group checks. The README describes FastAPI and Flask integration, a chat SSE endpoint, lifecycle hooks for quotas and logging, LLM middlewares for caching, conversation storage, and observability hooks. A pre-built web component is provided for embedding in React, Vue, or plain HTML pages.
use_cases: chat interface for querying a SQL database
multi-tenant SaaS with per-user data permissions
embedding a text-to-SQL chat widget in a web app
adding AI data Q&A to an existing FastAPI app
migrating from Vanna 0.x to the agent-based API
how_to_run: pip install vanna (implied by the Python imports; exact command not shown in the README)
Create a UserResolver subclass that extracts user identity and group memberships from requests
Create an LLM service (e.g. AnthropicLlmService) and a ToolRegistry with RunSqlTool bound to a database runner such as SqliteRunner
Create an Agent with llm_service, tool_registry, and user_resolver
Call register_chat_routes(app, ChatHandler(agent)) on your FastAPI app to expose POST /api/vanna/v2/chat_sse
Embed the web component in your frontend page
notable: User-aware permissions applied at the prompt, tool, and SQL-filtering layers, with per-user audit logs
Streams structured UI components (progress, SQL, table, chart, summary) to a pre-built web component
Supports many LLM providers and databases as listed in the README
Provides a LegacyVannaAdapter to wrap existing 0.x instances and a migration guide
Extensible via custom Tool classes, lifecycle hooks, and LLM middlewares
caveats: Major 2.0 rewrite; the README says the API differs from 0.x and requires migration
Row-level security, quotas, and audit logging are implemented by the user through hooks and resolvers, per the README's description
Enterprise support is referenced by email; some advanced features point to external full documentation not included in the README
